title: SARC Suite Unified Evidence Set line (v2)
description: One decision's unified Evidence Set line. v2 (independent review finding F2, review/REVIEW.md): remediation.evidence_substitution now additionally carries pre_evidence_ids (Phase I evidence ids) and substitute_source (buffer_key, content-addressed buffer_write_eid), so provenance can be identified and verified relative to a content-addressed store from the line alone -- see appendix-a-proofs.md's restated Proposition 4. v1 carried remediation phase records for BOTH remediators (evidence substitution and resource downroute) and the W1/W2 workflow tag, pre-registered in prereg/w2-workflow.md and prereg/renaming.md, implemented in Phase 2/3.

remediation.description: Phase records for both remediators. Each is null when that remediator did not trigger for this decision. evidence_substitution is meaningful in W1 and W2; downroute only ever triggers in W2 (Green SARC's Verdict.DOWNROUTE path, per prereg/w2-workflow.md).

pre_evidence_ids.description: Content-addressed ids (EvidenceRecord.evidence_id()) of the Phase I records the evidence gate actually evaluated before substitution -- identifies and allows verification of what was relied on, given the record store; it does not, by itself, reconstruct the original bytes (Proposition 4, restated).

substitute_source.description: Where the substituted value came from: the governed buffer's site key, and the id of the SPECIFIC durable write event the substitution actually drew from. Fixed per round-two independent review finding R2-F6(a): buffer_write_eid used to be a bare hash of (key, value) alone, so repeated identical writes -- common, since many SKUs' governed cost doesn't change often -- collapsed onto the SAME id (the review's provenance probe found 3,478 real substitution occurrences resolving to only 62 unique ids). buffer_write_eid now identifies exactly one entry in this run's durable, append-only governed-buffer write log (persisted next to the evidence lines as <scenario>-<mode>-buffer-writes.jsonl, one JSON object per line: write_seq, key, value, day, event_id -- event_id hashes all four together, so distinct write events always get distinct ids even when key and value repeat). Every entry in that log -- including a genesis entry per SKU seeded from the buffer's pre-run known-good values, for substitutions that trace back to that initial state rather than a write made during this run -- resolves buffer_write_eid to exactly one write-log line, never zero, never several (Appendix A, Proposition 4).

order_applied.description: Fixed declared remediator evaluation order actually used for this decision (per prereg/w2-workflow.md: evidence gate before resource gate). Empty array when neither remediator triggered.

dq.description: phase1_predicates and predicates are BOTH always present (both listed in required below) -- this schema has no 'missing' state for either, only 'present and possibly empty'. phase1_predicates is Phase I's firing record: whatever sarc_dq predicates matched the evidence as originally submitted, before any remediation. predicates is what Phase II actually judged the action on -- documented per round-two independent review finding R2-N4 (review-r2/REVIEW-R2.md): predicates is empty in two structurally different cases, and non-empty in a third. (1) Evidence was clean and unremediated: Phase I found nothing, and composition.py reuses Phase I's decision for Phase II as a no-op optimization (re-running would be redundant since the evidence didn't change) -- predicates equals phase1_predicates, both empty. (2) Evidence had a substitutable defect that WAS remediated: Phase II genuinely re-runs DQ evaluation on the post-remediation evidence, which is governed-clean by construction (Lemma 1, appendix-a-proofs.md) and so is found predicate-free -- predicates is empty while phase1_predicates records the original (non-empty) firing that triggered the substitution. (3) Evidence had a non-substitutable defect (dq gate's Phase I verdict was not 'substitute', e.g. an unremediable schema/lineage violation): nothing was remediated, so Phase II reuses Phase I's decision unchanged (same no-op path as case 1) -- predicates equals phase1_predicates, both non-empty, describing the same still-unresolved violation. An empty predicates array therefore never means 'Phase II did not run' in the sense of being skipped without judgment -- it certifies no predicate fired against whatever evidence Phase II actually judged (which case 1/3 show is sometimes literally Phase I's own evidence, reused rather than re-evaluated, and case 2 shows is sometimes freshly re-evaluated remediated evidence).

phase1_predicates.description: Phase I's firing record: sarc_dq predicates that matched the evidence as originally submitted, before any remediation. Always present; empty iff the original evidence was clean.

predicates.description: What Phase II actually judged the action on -- see the parent gates.dq object's description for the three cases (clean/unremediated, remediated-and-clean, non-substitutable-and-unremediated) that determine whether this is empty and, if non-empty, whether it equals phase1_predicates.

response.description: Lowercase restrictiveness-lattice response (Definition 1): admit < substitute < degrade < escalate < block.
